correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple G with n>=2 and m edges, reconstruct Q(S(G))-2I as [[D-2I,B],[B^T,0]], with unsigned incidence B. A rank-r saddle matrix has r positive and r negative directions plus inertia of C on ker B^T, and m-r null directions. Rank B=n for nonbipartite G, n-1 for bipartite G, where the residual quadratic form on the bipartition sign vector equals 2(m-n). The unsigned-incidence Gram transfer from Q(S(G)) to A(L(S(G)))+2I has m-n+1 extra zero Gram eigenvalues (hence extra -2 adjacency eigenvalues) but removes the one zero eigenvalue of Q; this yields exactly (n,m-n,m), (n-1,0,n-1), (n-1,2,n-1), or (n,m-n+1,m-1) in the stated mutually exhaustive cases. Boundary K2/tree, odd C5, even C4, bipartite bicyclic K2,3 independently had numerical inertias (1,0,1),(5,0,5),(3,2,3),(5,2,5); a P4 had (3,0,3). The arbitrary-n result is the congruence and incidence argument, not these finite spectra.
